title: Freya and the Horizon
premise: Rosalind 'Freya' Whitlock, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries under a name that isn't the one she was born with, is scraping by on the coast when an extreme low tide exposes a sea cave the locals have charged tourists to gawk at for a century. Inside, she finds a drowned survey map pointing to the source of the River Vane — a headwater sealed off by concession permits held by the company that ruined her reputation. When a wealthy expedition patron pulls her into his bid to reach the source before the permits expire in six weeks, Freya must lead a found family of misfits upriver through country designed to kill them, all while hiding both her past and the truth that the 'legend' is a cover for what her old mentor buried there. At the source she must choose between exposing the document that would clear her name and destroying it to protect the people who trusted her; she chooses loyalty, burns the proof, and walks out unnamed but unowned, her record intact only in the memories of those who now vouch for her.
about_author: Oscar Brightwater is the pen name of a former river-logging surveyor who spent eleven years guiding in fjord country before trading the water for the page. He writes adventure novels about people the wilderness refuses to either forgive or forget.

chapters.title: The Tide That Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Working as a dockhand under the name Freya, she watches the lowest tide in decades drain the bay and reveal a cave mouth locals call the Tollhouse. She enters alone against her own survival instincts. Emotional beat: restless hunger for a self that isn't hiding.

chapters.title: Admission Charged
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Inside the cave she finds a waterproofed survey case bearing her mentor Halvard's initials and a map to the Vane's forbidden source. A tour operator catches her leaving and blackmails her. Beat: dread — the past has literally surfaced.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Mountains
chapters.summary: POV Augustin Vale, aging expedition financier, arrives to buy out the concession before its permits lapse. He interviews local guides, dismisses them all, then recognizes something in 'Freya's' hands when she repairs his rope. Beat: being seen is dangerous.

chapters.title: Blacklisted Twice Over
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Flashback woven through present: how the Kestrel Pass disaster got her banned from two countries under her birth name, and why she let the world believe Rosalind Whitlock was finished. Beat: grief disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Six Weeks of Paper
chapters.summary: POV Augustin. He offers Freya lead-guide wages she can't refuse and admits the permits expire at season's end — after that, the source is legally sealed for twenty years. Beat: a bargain struck between two people concealing motives.

chapters.title: A Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She assembles the team: disgraced hydrologist Nils, teenage runaway cartographer Bee, and Vale's estranged nephew Tomas. First camp, first failures, first laughter. Beat: the fragile first stitches of found family.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: POV Bee. The crew enters the gorge; Freya's competence awes them, but Bee notices Freya navigating terrain she shouldn't know from maps alone. Beat: admiration shadowed by the first crack of suspicion.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gauge
chapters.summary: POV Nils. They find an abandoned gauging station with readings that contradict the official record — someone falsified the river data years ago, and the signature matches the Kestrel Pass report. Beat: Nils realizes the expedition is also an exhumation.

chapters.title: What Tomas Carries
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Vale's nephew confesses to Freya that his uncle funded the original falsified survey and wants the source reached to bury evidence, not find wonder. He begs her not to tell. Beat: loyalty vs. truth begins splitting the crew.

chapters.title: White Water, Old Wounds
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A rapids run nearly kills Bee; Freya's rescue is flawless but uses techniques only the blacklisted Whitlock ever taught. That night Nils says the name aloud. Beat: exposure, and the terror of being known.

chapters.title: The Confession at Cold Camp
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Around the fire she tells them everything — the pass disaster, the blacklist, Halvard's map. Instead of mutiny, they choose to stay. Beat: the found family holds, and it changes what her name means.

chapters.title: The Concession Men
chapters.summary: POV Augustin. Company rangers patrol the upper valley; the crew must move at night. Augustin privately burns a letter proving he knew the permits were a trap all along. Beat: the patron's mask slips for the reader, not yet the crew.

chapters.title: Bee's Map Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Bee. Her charts fail where the river goes underground; only Halvard's cave map can route them, forcing Freya to trust a dead man's hand over her own judgment. Beat: humility — even guides must be guided.

chapters.title: The Siphon
chapters.summary: POV Nils. The crew traverses the flooded tunnel beneath the falls; equipment and trust are both tested to breaking when Tomas freezes and Freya goes back for him. Beat: fear transmuted into fierce, wordless loyalty.

chapters.title: Halvard's Cache
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Above the falls they find her mentor's final camp: journals revealing he falsified nothing — he discovered the falsification and was silenced, and the source holds the original surveys. Beat: vindication that feels like a wound reopened.

chapters.title: What Clearing Your Name Costs
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. The documents would ruin dozens of families in the valley towns that live off the concession, including Bee's. Tomas argues for burning them; Freya calls him a coward and storms off. Beat: the central choice sharpened to a blade.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Permits expiring at dawn, they reach the headwater spring inside the mountain — beautiful, indifferent, holding the steel case with her exoneration. She stands before it as the others wait. Beat: stillness before the decision.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: POV Bee. Freya burns the originals but keeps Halvard's journal — the moral record, not the legal weapon. Augustin arrives too late to stop her and, unexpectedly, lets it go. Beat: sacrifice made visible; truth preserved as story, not leverage.

chapters.title: Descent in Anger
chapters.summary: POV Augustin. The company, tipped off, moves to arrest the crew for trespass; Augustin stalls the rangers with his remaining influence while the others run the river down. Beat: a compromised man spending his last credit well.

chapters.title: The Long Rapid Home
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The escape run through the gorge — every skill, every bond, every lesson paid forward in one sustained sequence. They make the lower river as the permit deadline passes. Beat: catharsis through motion.

chapters.title: Names Given Freely
chapters.summary: POV ensemble, anchored on Freya. In the valley town, the crew tells Halvard's true story publicly; the townspeople, owing their water's honesty to him, petition to lift the blacklist themselves. Beat: truth restored by community rather than paperwork.

chapters.title: Freya and the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Cleared but changed, she declines Augustin's offer to rebuild her old career and instead signs on to train the strays as guides. On the dock at high tide, the Tollhouse cave closes beneath the sea, keeping its last secret. Beat: identity chosen, family kept, horizon open.
